answer: An agent economy resists Sybils by requiring every identity to lock a slashable bond before participating. When peers detect correlated activity through a shared ledger anchor, the bond is burned. An attacker spinning up many fakes must therefore commit real capital that can vanish; the cost scales with each new identity, turning cheap clones into an expensive comet of lost value. A unique walnut-sized proof of continuous presence multiplies the expense and deters bulk creation.
